options: Describing a task with instructions only, with no worked examples included
Sending the same prompt zero times before giving up
A prompt that produces zero output tokens
Asking the model to generate its own examples first
questions.explain: Zero-shot relies entirely on the model's training to infer the task from a plain description, with no example input/output pairs.

questions.q: In the few-shot ticket-classification example, what do the two worked examples actually demonstrate beyond the category names?
options: Nothing extra — they just repeat the category list
The exact output format (one word, no punctuation) and how to resolve edge cases
The customer's account number format
How long the model's response should be in paragraphs
questions.explain: Worked examples show the precise format expected and demonstrate judgment calls that a plain instruction can't fully spell out.

questions.q: According to this lesson, roughly how many examples are usually enough for a few-shot prompt?
options: 20 to 30 examples
Exactly one example, never more
Two to five examples
As many as will fit in the context window
questions.explain: Two to five examples is typically enough; returns diminish fast beyond that, and extra examples mostly add tokens without improving consistency.

questions.q: Which of these is a good reason to use few-shot prompting instead of zero-shot?
options: The task needs an unusual, specific output format that's hard to describe in words
You want the prompt to use as few tokens as possible
The task is extremely simple and the model already gets it right every time
You want to avoid giving the model any context about the task
questions.explain: Few-shot is worth the extra tokens specifically when the format or judgment call is easier to show than to describe in words.

questions.q: What risk does this lesson associate with adding a poorly chosen example to a few-shot prompt?
options: It has no effect either way on the model's output
It automatically triggers an error from the model
It can mislead the model more than including no example at all
It always improves results regardless of quality
questions.explain: A badly chosen example can actively mislead the model's pattern-matching, making results worse than giving no example.
